name: card
title: Card
description: A bounded surface for grouped content, with parts you can restyle.
docs:
## When to use - A unit of content that belongs together: a summary, a plan, an account, a record in a grid. - A surface that needs a header, an optional action, body content, and a footer. - A list of comparable items where the boundary itself carries meaning. ## When not to use - To fake spacing. A card is a boundary; use padding if you only need breathing room. - As a page layout. Nesting cards inside cards flattens the hierarchy. - For a modal or a popover; those are overlays with their own focus rules. ## Installation ```bash npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/card ``` ## Usage ```tsx import { Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardFooter, CardHeader, CardTitle, } from "@/components/cadence/card/card"; import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button/button"; export function Plan() { return ( Parity plan 57 components, nine batches, one release train.

Batch B1 ships the eleven atoms.

 ); } ``` ## Examples ### Action in the header `CardHeader` switches to two columns when a `CardAction` is present — no extra prop, no manual grid. ```tsx Members 12 people have access. ``` ### Compact `size="sm"` tightens every part at once, because the spacing lives in one custom property on the root: ```tsx … ``` ### Section boundaries Add a rule with utilities rather than a new part; the `[.border-b]` selectors are already wired: ```tsx … … ``` ## API | Part | Props | Notes | | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | | `Card` | `size`, native div props | `size`: `"default" \| "sm"`. Sets `--card-spacing` and `data-size`. | | `CardHeader` | native div props | Grid header; reacts to `CardAction` and a bottom border. | | `CardTitle` | native div props | Bold, leading-none. Does not create a heading. | | `CardDescription` | native div props | Muted supporting text. | | `CardAction` | native div props | Top-right slot inside the header. | | `CardContent` | native div props | Body; carries the horizontal padding. | | `CardFooter` | native div props | Bottom row; reacts to a top border. | Every part sets `data-slot`, so CSS can reach it: `[&>[data-slot=card-header]]:gap-4`. ## Motion contract No motion (T0). A card does not fade, lift, or scale in. If a group of cards should appear in sequence, that is a page-level `list.stagger` decision made by the parent, not a property of the card. | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- | | – | none | – | – | | reduced | none | – | – | | none | none | – | – | ## Accessibility - `Card` is a plain `div`: no role, no landmark. That is correct for a visual grouping — but it means the card is not a navigable region. If a set of cards is the main content, wrap it in a `

    Parity plan

    `, or render the card with `aria-labelledby` pointing at the title's id. - A card that is clickable must contain a real link or button; do not put `onClick` on the card and call it done — it is invisible to keyboard users. ## Notes for AI - Use `CardFooter` for actions, not a bare `div` — it keeps spacing consistent when `size` changes. - Do not add hover lift to a card that is not interactive. Motion on a static card is decoration (P9).
